stem.en: Why can the lowest price on the board be a bad choice for a stall?

text.en: Visitors think a cheap drink is unsafe, so nobody buys it.
If the price is below the cost, each extra glass adds to the loss.
At the lowest price the drink tastes worse.
A low price always brings fewer people to the counter.

explanation.en: When the price is below the cost of making the drink, every glass sold loses money. Selling more glasses only makes the loss bigger, as at Stall A.

hints.en: Think about Stall A: a glass sold for ₹5 cost ₹6 to make.
